questions.text: Can you describe the place where you live?
questions.say: Good evening. My name is Lily, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about your home. Can you describe the place where you live?

cueCard.topic: Describe a building that you find attractive.
cueCard.explain: and explain why you find it attractive.

questions.text: Describe a building that you find attractive.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a building that you find attractive. You should say: where the building is; what it looks like; what it is used for; and explain why you find it attractive.

questions.text: Do other people also think this building is attractive?
questions.say: Thank you. Do other people also think this building is attractive?

questions.text: What kinds of buildings are most common in your city?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a building you find attractive, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all architecture. What kinds of buildings are most common in your city?

questions.text: Is it more important for a building to be beautiful or useful?
questions.say: Is it more important for a building to be beautiful or useful?

questions.text: Who should decide what new buildings look like?

questions.text: Should governments spend money on protecting old buildings?
questions.say: Now let's talk about old and new buildings. Should governments spend money on protecting old buildings?

questions.text: Why do some people prefer living in modern buildings?

questions.text: How do you think buildings will be different in fifty years?
